title: oryza sativa proles japonica
intro: Oryza sativa proles japonica, commonly known as Japanese rice, is a subspecies of Asian rice that belongs to the Poaceae family. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, which include lowering cholesterol levels, regulating blood sugar, and aiding in weight management. The therapeutic actions of Japanese rice are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), inositol, and ferulic acid, that exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-diabetic properties. The bioactive constituents of Japanese rice have also been found to have a potential therapeutic effect on cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's disease, and certain types of cancer.
